sn8.5:1.2: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn8.5:2.1: “Bhikkhus, when speech possesses four factors, then it is well spoken, not badly spoken, and it is blameless, not blameworthy among the wise.
sn8.5:2.3: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu speaks only what is well spoken, not what is badly spoken. He speaks only on the Dhamma, not on non-Dhamma. He speaks only what is pleasant, not what is unpleasant. He speaks only what is true, not what is false.
sn8.5:2.4: When speech possesses these four factors, it is well spoken, not badly spoken, and it is blameless, not blameworthy among the wise.”
sn8.5:2.5: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn8.5:2.6: Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this:
sn8.5:3.1: “What is well spoken, the good say, is foremost;
sn8.5:3.3: Third, speak what is pleasant, not unpleasant;
sn8.5:3.4: Fourth, speak the truth, not falsehood.”
sn8.5:4.1: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and, raising his joined hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One, said to him:
sn8.5:4.2: “An inspiration has come to me, Blessed One! An inspiration has come to me, Fortunate One!”
sn8.5:4.3: The Blessed One said: “Then express your inspiration, Vaṅgīsa.”
sn8.5:4.4: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Blessed One to his face with suitable verses
sn8.5:5.2: By which one does not afflict oneself
sn8.5:5.4: Such speech is truly well spoken.
sn8.5:6.3: When it brings them nothing evil
sn8.5:6.4: What one speaks is pleasant to others.
sn8.5:7.3: The goal and the Dhamma, the good say,
sn8.5:8.1: “The secure speech which the Buddha utters
sn8.5:8.3: For making an end to suffering
